summary: The Management appealed against the High Court's upholding of the Labour Court's award directing reinstatement and back wages to the respondent workman. Despite court-ordered attempts to serve notice and repeated communications for the respondent to report for duty—culminating in his counsel's assurance in 2007 that he would do so—the respondent failed to appear. The Supreme Court held that the respondent's conduct demonstrated lack of interest in rejoining service, warranting setting aside of the award and impugned orders on enforcement of back wages and continuity of service. The Court emphasized the necessity of furnishing permanent addresses by workmen in labour disputes to ensure effective service and relief, citing relevant procedural rules under various labour statutes.
legal_provisions_cited: Forms I, J, K, Industrial Dispute (Central) Rules, 1957
Order VI Rule 14A, Civil Procedure Code, 1908
Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
final_judgment: Appeal allowed. The impugned order of the High Court and the award of the Labour Court are set aside. The deposit of ₹10,000 shall be refunded to the appellant.
